data.claim: consume.operator_gate prefixes a refused Decision.message with 'refusing: ' on every path EXCEPT the auto=False/no-approval steering message, so callers recover refused-vs-steering from prose two different ways (config.set verbatim, phase_complete startswith sniff).
data.falsifier: operator_gate(auto=False, approval_id='') returns a message NOT starting with 'refusing: '.
data.mechanism: the steering branch (if not approval_id and not auto) builds its message without the prefix, while _checked, the filed-is-None branch and route all prefix it.
data.probe_output: pre-fix: FAILED (message = 'to ask the operator to approve ...' unprefixed). post-fix: PASSED.
data.question: Who owns the 'refusing: ' prefix on consume.Decision, and how do the callers encode the refused-vs-steering distinction?

evidence.note: Claim: the auto=False/no-approval steering message is the sole unprefixed refusal from operator_gate CONFIRMED (research R4fd664cc2c). Probe: test_operator_gate_owns_the_refusing_prefix_on_the_steering_refusal failed pre-fix ('to ask the operator to approve ...' unprefixed), passes post-fix.

Read applicable rules/decisions: r-gemini-key-load, the two prior doubled-prefix bugs (B-config-phase-doubled-refusing-prefix, B-approval-refusal-doubled-prefix) and B-consume-refusal-prefix-owner; the fix follows the established direction that operator_gate owns the prefix.

Prefix the steering refusal in consume.operator_gate; drop phase_complete's startswith sniff to verbatim pass-through; add regression test test_operator_gate_owns_the_refusing_prefix_on_the_steering_refusal; update stale comment in tests/test_approvals_sites_wired.py. Commit 0ec5c3e1e.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix leaves `config.py` using the old “unconditional-drop” handling described in B-consume-refusal-prefix-owner. After this change, `operator_gate` now returns `"refusing: to ask the operator to approve ..."` on the no-approval steering path, but `config.py` still unconditionally drops the `"refusing: "` prefix, so the config command emits `"to ask the operator to approve ..."` with no refusal marker. That is the same prose-as-structure bug this change is supposed to consolidate away, and the included regression test only exercises `phase_complete`, not `config.py`.

data.claim: It folds the negative exit into a failed command check ('exit -15'), recording ci=failed with no failing tests, because _result maps every p.code != 0 to 'failed'.
data.mechanism: _result builds Result('passed' if p.code == 0 else 'failed') and appends Check('command', False, 'exit {p.code}') for any nonzero (including negative) code.
data.question: How does the ci runner record a pre-commit run killed by a signal (negative exit code)?

evidence.note: Claim CONFIRMED (research R9f1942c8aa): _result maps every p.code != 0 (negative included) to 'failed'. Probe test_a_process_killed_by_a_signal_is_unavailable_not_failed fails pre-fix (status 'failed').

Read the ci run/gate exit-code rules and B512a5d7f35 (and its location on the ci runner _result). A killed process is unavailable (could not run/verdict), never a failure. Fix follows the existing unavailable mapping in _unfinished (timeout/not-ran).

In services/ci/runner._result, a negative p.code (killed by signal) now returns status 'unavailable' with reason 'killed by signal N' instead of 'failed'; added regression test test_a_process_killed_by_a_signal_is_unavailable_not_failed. Commit d96c6ed80.

chunk_findings.detail: The killed-signal branch sets `status="unavailable"`, but the line above still runs for negative exit codes: `if p.code != 0 and not any(not c.ok for c in checks): checks.append(Check("command", False, f"exit {p.code}"))`. For the exact bug input, `_result(CommandRun("ran", code=-15, out="ruff check.....................Passed"), ...)` now returns `status="unavailable"` but its `checks` list still contains `Check("command", False, "exit -15")`. Any consumer that treats `not c.ok` as a failed check — which is the representation this code itself uses for command failure — will still fold the signal into a failed check, so the bug is only half-fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py:623

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test's docstring promises “not a failed check that folds the killed hook into 'exit -15'” and “no failing tests,” but the test never inspects `res.checks` or `res.failures`; it only asserts `status == "unavailable"` and the reason text. Since the fixed code still creates the failed `Check("command", False, "exit -15")`, the test passes while the central failure mode remains, making it too weak to catch the incomplete fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `not killed` guard only inspects the final `p` passed to `_result`; it never uses `scope.unran`, even though `_run` now records a killed `selected` stage there and then still runs the trailing `always` stage. Given a run with selected and always tests where `selected` is SIGTERM-killed (`p.code == -15`, so `unran == {"selected"}`) and the later `always` process exits 0, `_result(p_always, ...)` sets `killed = False`. Control enters the loop at line 626, sees `scope.ok["selected"] is False`, and line 630 appends `Check("selected tests (N files)", False)` for a stage the change itself defines as “not a failure.” The returned `Result` is not `unavailable`, and it still contains a failed check for the killed stage, so the fix does not cover the case where a killed stage is followed by a later non-killed stage.
